entries.title: Νότια Κορέα παρακολουθεί επίσκεψη Κιμ στην Κίνα
entries.paragraph_1: Η Νότια Κορέα παρακολουθεί στενά την αναφερόμενη επίσκεψη του Κιμ Γιονγκ Ουν στην Κίνα, χωρίς ακόμη επίσημη επιβεβαίωση από Πεκίνο και Πιονγκγιάνγκ. Η Σεούλ αφήνει ανοικτά όλα τα ενδεχόμενα, αντιμετωπίζοντας το ταξίδι ως κίνηση με σαφές διπλωματικό βάρος στην περιοχή. Η Νότια Κορέα παρακολουθεί στενά τις πληροφορίες για αιφνιδιαστική επίσκεψη του Κιμ Γιονγκ Ουν στην Κίνα, αναγνωρίζοντας ότι κάθε μετακίνηση του Βορειοκορεάτη ηγέτη έχει άμεση επίπτωση στις ισορροπίες ασφαλείας στην κορεατική χερσόνησο. Το προεδρικό γραφείο στη Σεούλ, το γνωστό «Μπλε Σπίτι», επιβεβαίωσε ότι εξετάζει «πολλαπλά σενάρια» καθώς δεν υπάρχει ακόμη επίσημη ανακοίνωση από Πεκίνο ή Πιονγκγιάνγκ. Ποια σενάρια εξετάζει η Νότια Κορέα για την κινεζική επίσκεψη; Σύμφωνα με κυβερνητικούς παράγοντες, η Σεούλ βλέπει την αναφερόμενη μετάβαση του Κιμ στην παραμεθόρια πόλη Νταντόνγκ ως πιθανή ένδειξη εντατικοποίησης της επαφής Πιονγκγιάνγκ – Πεκίνου. Η πιθανή συνάντηση με τον Κινέζο πρωθυπουργό Λι Τσιανγκ, ακόμη και σε σύντομο χρονικό πλαίσιο αυθημερόν επιστροφής, εκλαμβάνεται ως μήνυμα ότι η Κίνα διατηρεί ενεργό ρόλο ως βασικός συνομιλητής του βορειοκορεατικού καθεστώτος. Το «Μπλε Σπίτι» υπογραμμίζει ότι η απουσία επίσημων ανακοινώσεων δυσχεραίνει την άμεση αξιολόγηση των προθέσεων των δύο πλευρών, ωστόσο η Νότια Κορέα αντιμετωπίζει την κίνηση ως μέρος ενός ευρύτερου παζλ περιφερειακής ασφάλειας. Η Σεούλ εμφανίζεται προσεκτική στο δημόσιο λόγο της, ώστε να μην προκαταλάβει το περιεχόμενο των συνομιλιών, αλλά ταυτόχρονα επιχειρεί να διαβάσει αν πίσω από το ταξίδι κρύβονται εξελίξεις σε θέματα πυρηνικού προγράμματος ή οικονομικής στήριξης της Βόρειας Κορέας. Πώς εντάσσεται η κίνηση στο περιφερειακό πλαίσιο ισχύος; Η επιλογή της Νταντόνγκ, βασικής πύλης εμπορίου Κίνας – Βόρειας Κορέας, υπενθυμίζει ότι η οικονομική διάσταση παραμένει κρίσιμη για την αντοχή του βορειοκορεατικού καθεστώτος. Σε μια περίοδο αυξημένων εντάσεων στην Ανατολική Ασία, κάθε ένδειξη ενίσχυσης των δεσμών Πιονγκγιάνγκ – Πεκίνου επηρεάζει τον υπολογισμό κινδύνου της Σεούλ αλλά και τον σχεδιασμό των Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών στην περιοχή. Για τη Νότια Κορέα, η στενή παρακολούθηση τέτοιων κινήσεων δεν είναι τυπική διπλωματική άσκηση, αλλά βασικό εργαλείο έγκαιρης προειδοποίησης για πιθανές ανατροπές στο καθεστώς κυρώσεων ή σε στρατιωτικές ισορροπίες. Η στάση αναμονής που επιδεικνύει σήμερα η Σεούλ προϊδεάζει για εντατικές διαβουλεύσεις με συμμάχους, εφόσον η επίσκεψη επιβεβαιωθεί και αποσαφηνιστεί το περιεχόμενό της. Τι σημαίνει για την Ελλάδα Για την Ελλάδα, κάθε κίνηση που αναβαθμίζει τον ρόλο της Κίνας ως βασικού συνομιλητή της Βόρειας Κορέας ενισχύει τη γεωπολιτική βαρύτητα του Πεκίνου σε όλα τα διεθνή φόρα όπου συμμετέχει και η Αθήνα. Σε ένα περιβάλλον αυξανόμενης πόλωσης, η Αθήνα καλείται να παρακολουθεί προσεκτικά πώς τέτοιες περιφερειακές διεργασίες επηρεάζουν τις ισορροπίες στο Συμβούλιο Ασφαλείας και στους διεθνείς οργανισμούς όπου συζητούνται ζητήματα ασφάλειας και μη διάδοσης. Σχόλιο : Η προσεκτική στάση της Νότιας Κορέας αναδεικνύει πόσο κρίσιμη είναι η έγκαιρη ανάγνωση κινήσεων σε κλειστά καθεστώτα, στοιχείο που αφορά άμεσα και την ελληνική διπλωματία στις τοποθετήσεις της για ζητήματα ασφάλειας στην Ασία. Η Αθήνα έχει συμφέρον να αξιοποιεί τέτοιες εξελίξεις για να ενισχύει τον ρόλο της ως προβλέψιμου, θεσμικού συνομιλητή εντός της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης και του ΝΑΤΟ. (AP Photo/Ahn Young-joon) (AP Photo/Ahn Young-joon) SEOUL, South Korea (AP) — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited China on Saturday, inaugurating a new bridge that connects the two countries and saying he hoped to expand cooperation with his powerful neighbor. Kim’s visit to China is his latest move in an increasingly assertive foreign policy as he seeks to align Pyongyang with Beijing and Moscow in a united front against the United States under what he portrays as a “new Cold War.” It’s his first visit in a year. Kim arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong Saturday after crossing the newly opened bridge , according to South Korea’s Unification Ministry, which handles affairs related to North Korea, and China’s official Xinhua News Agency. Both sides promised to strengthen cooperation He met with Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of China’s Communist Party. The two toured a car factory, and promised to strengthen the bilateral relationship. Kim said his country “stands ready to work with China to carry forward their historical friendship and expand practical cooperation, thereby delivering tangible benefits to the peoples of both countries,” Xinhua said. Wang then accompanied Kim to the bridge to send him off, according to Xinhua. North Korean state media did not immediately report on Kim’s visit. New bridge was built to help expand trade between the countries Experts said the opening of the New Yalu River Bridge this month was a key symbol of strengthening ties between North Korea and China and reflected their intent to expand trade, as it is expected to accommodate two-way traffic around the clock, including container shipments and heavy cargo trucks. Kim has recently sought to strengthen ties with China, the North’s traditional main ally and economic lifeline, after years of prioritizing ties with Russia. He sent thousands of troops and conventional weapons to support President Vladimir Putin’s war in Ukraine , possibly in exchange for military and economic assistance. Kim’s visit timed to key battle anniversary in Korean War with China Kim’s latest visit to China is his sixth since taking power in late 2011 following the death of his father. The visit appears to be timed to underscore the strength of his ties with Beijing ahead of the Oct. 25 anniversary of China’s first major victory in the Korean War, which was days after Chinese troops crossed the Yalu River into North Korea in October 1950. The war began with North Korea’s surprise attack on the South in June 1950, prompting a U.N.-led coalition headed by the United States to intervene and push back the offensive. North Korea was backed primarily by Chinese forces, with assistance from the then-Soviet Union’s air force, before fighting ended with a 1953 armistice that left the peninsula technically at war. Kim said his visit on Saturday was also to memorialize those killed in the war, according to Xinhua. Chinese President Xi Jinping traveled to Pyongyang in June for a meeting with Kim. During their summit , Xi expressed Beijing’s willingness to expand bilateral cooperation in trade, agriculture, construction and technology, while Kim described ties with China as a top strategic priority. Kim last visited Beijing in September 2025, when he met with Xi and watched a military parade alongside Putin and other foreign leaders. Kim has maintained a hard line toward Seoul and has so far rebuffed a proposal from U.S. President Donald Trump to revive their diplomacy, which broke down in 2019 during Trump’s first term. Kim’s government has called for Washington to abandon its “hostile policy” and drop demands for the North’s denuclearization as a precondition for renewed talks. South Korea’s liberal government, which favors engagement with the North, hopes renewed talks between Washington and Pyongyang will thaw inter-Korean relations, and has also urged China to play a “constructive” role in resolving the standoff. Seoul’s spy agency told lawmakers last month that it saw a 50% possibility of a meeting between Trump and Kim on the sidelines of next month’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, or APEC, summit in Shenzhen, China. “From Seoul’s perspective, if North Korea focuses more on economic development than military buildup and threats, that would be positive for diplomacy and security,” said Leif-Eric Easley, a professor at Ewha University in Seoul. “But if Kim can extract ever more benefits from China and Russia, it is unclear what Seoul could offer that would be worth the political risks Pyongyang attaches to exchanges with a more prosperous, globalized, and free Korea.” ___ Wu reported from Bangkok. entries.paragraph_1: عمون - قترحت كوريا الجنوبية الجمعة على كوريا الشمالية إجراء محادثات عسكرية بشأن مسار خط ترسيم الحدود في وسط المنطقة المنزوعة السلاح التي تفصل بينهما، بعد حوادث خطيرة عديدة، وفق ما أعلنت وزارة الدفاع. وأفاد نائب وزير الدفاع كيم هونغ شيول خلال مؤتمر صحافي في سيول إن كوريا الجنوبية "تعرض رسميا عقد مفاوضات عسكرية مع كوريا الشمالية للتأكيد المتبادل لموقع خط التماس العسكري البري بدقة وبحث سبل معاودة خطوط التواصل العسكرية ومنع وقوع مواجهات عرضية في المناطق الحدودية". وقال المسؤول إنه "يمكن مناقشة التواريخ والمواقع المحددة عبر بانمونجوم"، نقطة التواصل الوحيدة بين الكوريتين في وسط المنطقة المنزوعة السلاح التي تفصل بينهما. وتابع أن سيول "تأمل في ردّ إيجابي من كوريا الشمالية"، مشيرا إلى أن المحادثات يمكن أن تضم قيادة الأمم المتحدة، القوة المتعددة الجنسيات بقيادة الولايات المتحدة المنتشرة في كوريا الجنوبية. وقطعت كوريا الشمالية كلّ الاتصالات مع كوريا الجنوبية منذ سنوات، ولا تزال حتى الآن تتجاهل دعوات الرئيس الكوري الجنوبي لي جاي ميونغ، المؤيد بقوة لاستئناف الحوار بين الكوريتين. وبدأت بيونغ يانغ منذ عام 2023 تحصين جانبها من المنطقة المنزوعة السلاح، وهي منطقة عازلة أُنشئت عند انتهاء الحرب الكورية (1950-1953)، متخلية عن أي أفق لإعادة توحيد شبه الجزيرة الكورية، وباتت تعتبر الجنوب دولة معادية. entries.paragraph_1: La tensión militar entre las dos Coreas ha alcanzado un punto crítico tras cruzarse nuevas amenazas directas sobre el estatus operacional de su frontera común. El detonante directo de esta última escalada radica en la investigación oficial del Mando de las Naciones Unidas, la cual concluyó que las explosiones de minas registradas el pasado 21 de septiembre en la Zona Desmilitarizada (DMZ) —que provocaron heridas graves a tres soldados surcoreanos— fueron causadas por artefactos sembrados deliberadamente por las fuerzas de Pyongyang. Tras la exigencia formal de disculpas por parte del Gobierno de Seúl liderado por el presidente Lee Jae-myung , el régimen norcoreano no solo ha rechazado tajantemente cualquier autoría en el suceso, sino que ha tildado las conclusiones occidentales de "farsa inventada" utilizada como pretexto para violar su soberanía territorial.

La influyente dirigente advirtió de que la situación en la frontera meridional es "muy inestable" debido al "comportamiento imprudente de los militares títeres" del Sur.

entries.title: From Soviet-era UAZ to Aurus limousines: Russian cars used by foreign leaders
entries.paragraph_1: For decades, Russian and Soviet automotive exports have served as more than just transportation tools for foreign heads of state; they have functioned as diplomatic instruments and, in some cases, enduring symbols of geopolitical alignment. From the rugged utility of the UAZ-469B to the modern prestige of the Aurus Senat, the interaction between Russian vehicle manufacturers and international leaders reveals a complex dynamic where engineering capability, political signaling, and logistical realities intersect.
entries.paragraph_2: The historical precedent for this relationship dates back to the Cold War, when the Soviet government gifted an open-top, rear-wheel-drive UAZ-469B, a vehicle originally designed for military command, to Kim Il-sung, the leader of North Korea. This gesture established a pattern of reliance that persisted through generations. In 2018, his grandson, Kim Jong-un, arrived at a summit with the South Korean leader in a heavily armored Mercedes-Maybach, a clear indicator of a shift in the preferred status symbols of the North Korean regime. However, reports indicate that the North Korean leader's private garage also contains new models of the UAZ Patriot, suggesting that the brand has retained a functional place in the national fleet despite the availability of German luxury alternatives.

entries.title: Aumenta tensión en la frontera de Pyongyang y Corea del Sur | AlMomento.net - Noticias de República Dominicana al instante!
entries.paragraph_1: Escuchar artículo Reproducir Pausar Detener SEUL 21 Oct.- Las autoridades de Corea de Norte han alertado este miércoles de que «no habrá compasión» con Corea del Sur en caso de que su «seguridad territorial» o su «personal» desplegado en la frontera sufra algún daño, unas declaraciones que llegan en pleno aumento de la tensión entre las partes. Kim Yo Jong, alto cargo del Partido del Trabajo de Corea y hermana del líder norcoreano, Kim Jong Un, ha indicado en un comunicado que «no habrá piedad alguna para los gánsters armados y faltos de razón», según informaciones recogidas por la agencia estatal de noticias norcoreana KCNA. Así se ha pronunciado tras inspeccionar la frontera junto a altos cargos del Ejército, una zona que ha asegurado que se encuentra «bloqueada» tras ser «transformada en una fortaleza». «Esto muestra que estamos garantizando la seguridad de Corea del Norte de cara al futuro», ha expresado. «Nuestro Ejército está poniendo en marcha medidas de vital importancia frente a las continuadas amenazas del enemigo; pronto empezará una nueva historia de paz. Si la frontera se fortifica, el peligro a un conflicto militar en esta zona quedará completamente eliminado, sin lugar a dudas», ha sostenido. Además, ha afirmado que las «unidades tácticas» de las fuerzas norcoreanas se están reposicionando para volver a colocar los altavoces en la frontera para la difusión de propaganda. «Estarán operativos en toda esa zona», ha apuntado, al tiempo que ha reivindicado esta medida como «justa» y «necesaria». «Estamos preparados para cualquier imprevisto, manteniendo una gran contención», ha asegurado, no sin antes criticar duramente el uso de este tipo de altavoces por parte de Corea del Sur y la realización de disparos en varios puntos de la frontera. «Supongamos que, ante una situación como la de hoy, respondiéramos al fuego enemigo a modo de advertencia. La situación a lo largo de la frontera escalaría hasta alcanzar una fase de una gravedad inimaginable», ha lamentado. La tensión entre las partes ha vuelto a aumentar recientemente a raíz de la explosión de varias minas el pasado mes de septiembre en la Zona Desmilitarizada, donde tres militares surcoreanos resultaron heridos. Seúl ha acusado reiteradamente a Pyongyang de estar detrás de las explosiones –causadas por minas antipersona–, si bien Corea del Norte sigue negando cualquier implicación. El Gobierno surcoreano ha acusado a las autoridades norcoreanas de tratar de «agravar» la situación e intentar culpar a Seúl del aumento de las tensiones, habida cuenta de los intentos de acercamiento puestos en marcha desde que el presidente, Lee Jae Myung, llegó al cargo. Así, ha defendido en todo momento que los disparos de advertencia realizados son «legítimos y defensivos», destinados a «impedir que las tropas norcoreanas violen la línea de demarcación militar y repeler a aquellos soldados que la crucen». of-am Compártelo en tus redes:

entries.title: Oakland Coal Terminal Backed by Trump Would Be Bigger, Dirtier Than Promised, Says Report | Post News Group
entries.paragraph_1: By Post Staff A recent feasibility study commissioned by potential investors says an Oakland coal terminal backed by President Donald Trump could export 13 million tons a year — three times the amount estimated in an earlier environmental review. Surprisingly, the report also contradicts developers’ and project advocates’ repeated pledges that the coal would be stored in a covered terminal. Instead, the millions of tons of coal shipped annually from inland states to the West Gateway terminal in Oakland would be stored in “two open-air bunkers,” with about 150,000 tons of coal per stockpile, before being sent overseas, according to the recent report cited by the L.A. Times. ( https://ruic.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Port-Study-RUIC-Bulk-Commodity-Ocean-Terminals-Study.pdf ) Residents and clean air advocates have long expressed concerns that coal dust would worsen pollution in West Oakland and throughout the East Bay. The proposed site of the Oakland Bulk and Oversized Terminal (OBOT) is located at the former Army base near the Port of Oakland, which developer Phil Tagami has been trying for years to turn into a shipping terminal despite determined community opposition. Trump announced a $75-million investment in the project in June , about a third of its estimated cost. The new terminal would be the largest coal export site on the West Coast, transporting coal to Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and Malaysia, according to the Trump administration. Trending Oakland Mural Project on the Rise Opponents say a new terminal would undermine years of progress cleaning up the air in West Oakland, which has a history of disproportionate pollution and high asthma rates due to its proximity to the port and other industry. According to No Coal in Oakland organizer Ted Franklin, who has been active for 11 years in the fight to stop the coal terminal, the report indicates that investors may be looking for a cheaper way to build the terminal. “We were shocked but not surprised” by the report, Franklin said. “Basically, it seems that the plan now is to store open piles of coal, which is a less expensive project than creating a completely enclosed facility.” The threats that the project poses are real, but it faces a lot of economic and legal hurdles, he said. Coal production is in permanent decline worldwide, he said, wondering who was going to “invest money in an industry that has no future.” Further, the project has not yet attracted big investors. “There’s no bank, no financing, no financial institution backing this,” he continued. A major legal hurdle facing the project is the passage of Assemblymember Mia Bonta’s bill, AB 40, the Community-First Coal Review Act, signed into law by Gov. Gavin Newsom on Sept. 30. The law requires developers of large-volume bulk coal facilities to complete a full Environmental Impact Report (EIR) under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) before they can operate. The law was specifically designed to block or delay the coal terminal project. The report to potential developers was produced by consulting groups Norda Stelo and Wood Mackenzie in July and released this month. It was commissioned by the Rural Utah Infrastructure Coalition, made up of eight Utah counties that are considering investing about $43 million into the terminal to receive Utah coal. The consultants produced their findings after visiting Oakland, examining engineering documents and holding discussions with Savage Cos., a Utah-based transport and logistics company selected to operate the facility Research has shown that coal terminal operations can be dangerous to public health. The ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach moved away from open-air coal and petroleum coke storage three decades ago. The report says that the site could process 12 million metric tons, or 13.2 million tons, of coal each year, three times more than the terminal’s approved environmental impact report from 2002 and its 2012 addendum. Neither document mentions coal specifically, but rather bulk commodities. The coal arriving in Oakland could also be dirtier then had been previously stated, according to the report. Project officials previously said the terminal would handle only high-grade western bituminous coal from Utah, but the recent report says it will also handle Powder River Basin coal from Wyoming and Montana, known to be much dustier. Nor does the report mention plans to cover the rail cars to prevent pollution, though project officials previously promised they would only utilize coal transported in covered rail cars. “It appears the developers want to build something much bigger and more polluting than anything they previously revealed, either in court or to the West Oakland community,” said Colin O’Brien, deputy managing attorney at the nonprofit Earthjustice, speaking to the L.A. Times. The report indicates that the project may be much more expensive and take longer to complete than anticipated. The Energy Department estimates the terminal will cost about $231 million, but the report places the price at between $430 million and $625 million. The terminal will take 53 months to complete according to the report, significantly longer than Trump’s promise of exports beginning in 2028. Ted Franklin’s column, “Utah Study Blesses Investment in Oakland Coal Terminal but Leaves Key Questions Unanswered” is available at https://nocoalinoakland.info/utah-study-blesses-investment-in-oakland/ Post News Group Posts by Post News Group

entries.title: US cannot provide South Korea with self-reliant defense it seeks - China Military
entries.paragraph_1: Gen. Xavier Brunson, commander of the US Forces Korea (USFK), recently sparked strong domestic backlash in South Korea after making controversial remarks at an event in the United States. Brunson stated that the conditions for transferring wartime operational control (OPCON) to South Korea had shifted, necessitating "new standards." The South Korean Ministry of National Defense promptly expressed deep concern, with its spokesperson bluntly stating that if the goalposts keep moving, OPCON can never be transferred.
entries.paragraph_2: On the surface, this controversy involves issues of national sovereignty and OPCON transfer, but in essence, it reflects deep-seated contradictions in modernizing the ROK-US alliance: South Korea hopes to leverage alliance modernization to achieve self-reliant defense, while the US seeks to exploit South Korea's drive for defense autonomy to fold it more deeply into its regional strategic posture. Although the two sides seem to be heading in the same direction, their actual strategic objectives are misaligned.

entries.paragraph_2: Most frequently, the “thing other than technical maturity” is policy.
